title: applied-ml-eval-framework-and-playbooks-2026
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's Applied ML evaluation framework and associated playbooks. It consolidates guidance and operational procedures for: the eval harness, prompt set and benchmark management, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile usage, and regression triage. The goal is to ensure consistent quality checks, repeatable triage, and low-friction onboarding for model variants destined for serving.

Scope and audience

- Scope: evaluation processes that gate model onboarding, periodic quality monitoring, and regression response for models used in Redwood hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Audience: ML engineers, applied ML, model ops, reliability engineers, and product owners.

1) Eval Harness: architecture, onboarding, and regression runs

Summary
- The eval harness (service: eval-harness) is Redwood's standardized evaluation runner that executes deterministic prompt suites, computes metrics, and outputs artifacts (metrics.json, diffs, screenshots). It supports local CI runs, scheduled benchmarks, and on-demand regressions.

Components
- Runner: Python-based orchestrator (repository: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness).
- Storage: S3 bucket s3://redwood-eval-artifacts for run outputs and baselines.
- Scheduler: Airflow DAGs for nightly and canary runs (dag ids: eval_nightly, eval_canary).
- Reporter: Slack + PagerDuty integration for high-severity regressions.

Onboarding checklist for new evaluators (short):
1. Create a new evaluator entry in evaluations.yaml with fields: id, owner, description, input_schema, metrics, and required_prompts.
2. Add canonical prompt-set under prompt-sets/<evaluator-id>.json and register in prompt registry (tooling: prompt-registry-cli).
3. Provide gold labels or scoring function and include examples (min 200 examples for open-domain tasks; 1k recommended for high-risk tasks).
4. Add baseline artifacts to s3://redwood-eval-baselines/<evaluator-id>/<model-version>/metrics.json.
5. Run local harness: python -m eval_harness.run --evaluator <id> --model <model_uri> and verify artifact upload.
6. Request review from reviewers team and assign an owner in the evaluations.yaml.

Best practices
- Keep evaluators small and focused (max 5 metrics per evaluator unless aggregation required).
- Prefer deterministic prompts; annotate any stochastic behavior.
- Version prompts alongside evaluators. Use semantic version tags (v1.0.0).

2) Prompt sets and benchmarks

Naming and storage conventions
- Prompt files: prompt-sets/<task-slug>/<prompt-set-name>-v<semver>.jsonl. Each record: {"id", "input", "metadata"}.
- Benchmarks: bench-results/<benchmark-slug>/<model-version>/<run-timestamp>/metrics.json.

Coverage matrix
- Every publicly served model must be covered by: safety baseline, hallucination baseline (for generation models), at least 3 product-specific prompt sets, and at least 1 adversarial prompt set.

Metric guidance
- Metrics must be numeric; preferred metrics include Exact Match, BLEU/ROUGE (for structured outputs), BLEU-like similarity with thresholded acceptance, accuracy, F1, and calibrated confidence-rate.
- Always include per-prompt and aggregate metrics, plus 95th and 99th percentile latency for the harness run.

Example CI snippet (YAML)
- name: Run evaluator
  uses: redwood/actions/run-eval@v1
  with:
    evaluator-id: "dialog-quality-v1"
    model-uri: "redwood://models/xy-model/1.2.0"

3) Model onboarding guide (applies to open and internal models)

Acceptance criteria summary
- Performance: must not regress core product metrics by >2% relative to baseline (see product-specific SLA doc).
- Quality: passes all high-severity evaluators (defined per product) and no more than 1 medium-severity regression.
- Latency: 95p token latency within model family budget (e.g., 95p <= 250ms for chat-optimized small models; <= 800ms for large opt).
- Cost: per-token inference cost within expected range or justification provided.

Onboarding steps (detailed)
1. Create an onboarding PR in repo evaluations/onboarding/<model-slug>. The PR must include: model card, quantization profile, evaluation manifest, and CI linkage.
2. Run full eval harness against: canary cluster, nightly benchmark, and adversarial suites.
3. Review results with product owner and applied-ml reviewer. Document sign-off with a CONCURRENCE tag in PR description.
4. Create a rollout plan (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% across 72h windows) and define automatic rollback triggers (see Rollout triggers).
5. After successful canary, publish model into the model catalog and pin baseline artifacts.

Required artifacts in onboarding PR
- model_card.md (owner, intended use, limitations, training data summary).
- evaluations/manifest.json (list of evaluators and expected thresholds).
- quantization-profile.yaml (see section 5).
- performance-profile.json (latency percentiles, throughput at batch sizes).

Rollout triggers (examples)
- Immediate rollback: any high-severity evaluator fails (severity mapping defined in quality guardrails).
- Conditional rollback: >3 medium regressions OR +5% increase in 95p latency relative to baseline.

4) Quality guardrails and alerting

Guardrail levels and mappings
- Severity: high | medium | low.
- High: safety violations, data leakage, catastrophic hallucination on labeled prompts. Action: PagerDuty P0, automatic rollback if during rollout.
- Medium: degradation of accuracy by >5% on product-critical evaluators, or 95p latency increase >10%. Action: Slack alert to #applied-ml, follow triage playbook within 4 hours.
- Low: minor metric drift (<5%) or cosmetic changes. Action: ticket in JIRA, monitor.

Monitoring and alerting targets
- Eval-run cadence: nightly full-suite, canary on-deploy, weekly adversarial.
- Alert thresholds: high severity triggers pagerduty; medium -> slack + JIRA.
- Dashboard requirements: per-evaluator time-series, per-prompt error heatmap, and model diff viewer.

Automated checks (CI gates)
- CI must block PR merge if any high-severity evaluator fails or >2 medium regressions are detected.
- Use the eval-checker tool to summarize diffs: eval-checker --baseline s3://redwood-eval-baselines/<id>/<version>/metrics.json --candidate ./metrics.json

5) Quantization profiles and guidance

Purpose
- Quantization profiles define per-operator and per-layer settings that balance accuracy and inference cost. Profiles are recommended for each model family and hardware class.

Profile format (YAML snippet)
- name: qprofile-gptx-int8
  model_family: gptx
  target_hardware: a100-pcie
  global_bits: 8
  per_layer_overrides: ["attn_layer_0:16", "ffn_layer_6:8"]
  calibration_dataset: s3://redwood-quant-calibration/gptx-small/v1

Recommended profile examples
- Small chat models (gptx-small): int8 global, attn-layer 16-bit for stability.
- Medium generators (gptx-medium): int8 with KL calibration and activation-aware per-layer overrides.
- LLM-XL (>70B): mixed 16/8 or Q4_0 depending on target throughput and accuracy.

Validation checklist
1. Run quantization pipeline: tools/quantize.py --profile quantization-profile.yaml --model <model-uri> --out <artifact-uri>.
2. Execute regression evaluators: run eval-harness for top 10 product evaluators and ensure no high-severity regressions.
3. Compare logits-level drift and downstream metric drift; store artifacts under s3://redwood-quant-results/<model-version>/.

6) Regression triage playbook

Runbook summary (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage lead acknowledges incident in PagerDuty and creates an incident issue [incident-<ts>] in JIRA with initial tags: regression, eval, model-slug, severity.
2. Gather evidence: attach latest metrics.json, diff report from eval-checker, and model-version metadata (git sha, quantization profile).
3. Reproduce locally: run the failing evaluator against baseline and candidate in isolated environment (docker image: redwood/eval-runner:stable).
4. Determine scope: single prompt set vs broad regression. Use prompt heatmap to localize high-error prompts.

Assessment and mitigation steps (60–240 minutes)
- If caused by model change: roll back to previous model baseline immediately and trigger a follow-up postmortem.
- If caused by quantization: revert to non-quantized variant or apply per-layer override patch and re-run target evaluators.
- If caused by prompt/regression in production routing: apply routing rule to route affected traffic to fallback model variant and schedule hotfix deployment.

Postmortem and follow-up
- Owner writes postmortem within 5 business days. Include timeline, root cause, remediation, and preventative actions.
- Required items: updated evaluators or prompt sets if gap identified, updated quantization profiles, and improved CI checks if regression could have been caught earlier.

7) Ownership, SLAs, and governance

- Ownership: Each evaluator must have a named owner (evaluations.yaml). The Applied ML team maintains central registry and CI tooling.
- SLOs for eval infrastructure: harness availability 99.9% (monthly), artifact upload success rate >= 99.5%.
- Governance: any change to high-severity evaluators requires at least two reviewers (one applied-ml, one product owner).

Appendix: example artifacts and commands

Example evaluations.yaml entry:
- id: "dialog-quality-v1"
  owner: "asha.patel@redwood.ai"
  description: "Evaluates turn-level relevance and factuality for chat flows"
  metrics: ["turn_f1", "hallucination_rate"]
  severity_mapping: {"hallucination_rate":"high"}

Run eval locally:
python -m eval_harness.run --evaluator dialog-quality-v1 --model redwood://models/xy-model/1.2.0 --output ./out; aws s3 cp ./out s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/dialog-quality-v1/1.2.0/ --recursive

Compare candidate vs baseline:
eval-checker --baseline s3://redwood-eval-baselines/dialog-quality-v1/1.1.0/metrics.json --candidate ./out/metrics.json --thresholds evaluations/thresholds.json

Contact and escalation
- Primary: Applied ML on-call (#applied-ml-oncall)
- PagerDuty: PD escalation policy 'applied-ml-regressions'
- Slack channels: #applied-ml, #model-rollouts
